# fossa-mcp — read-only MCP server for the FOSSA API (software composition
# analysis: projects, revisions, dependencies, licensing/vulnerability/quality
# issues, attribution reports). Nine tools, none of which mutate FOSSA state.
# Source: iCloud Developer/fossa-mcp (Apache-2.0, unofficial — not affiliated
# with FOSSA, Inc.).
#
# Image is built locally and imported into containerd, same as docs-rag-mcp:
#   docker build -t localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 .
#   docker save localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 | sudo k3s ctr -n k8s.io images import -
# Swap to docker.io/rashford/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 + pullPolicy IfNotPresent once that
# image is actually published (it is not, as of this commit).
#
# The FOSSA_API_TOKEN Secret is referenced by name and created out-of-band —
# see fossa-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: fossa-mcp
  name: fossa-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: fossa-mcp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fossa-mcp
    spec:
      containers:
      - args:
        - --transport
        - streamable-http
        env:
        # The image defaults to 127.0.0.1 by design (see the project's
        # DECISIONS.md §2). In a pod that would be unreachable through the
        # Service, so it binds the pod IP instead. Everything that can reach
        # this ClusterIP gets the full read access of the one token below —
        # there is no per-caller auth. Keep it ClusterIP-only.
        - name: FOSSA_HTTP_HOST
          value: 0.0.0.0
        # 8080 to match the other MCP servers in this namespace; the image
        # itself defaults to 8000.
        - name: FOSSA_HTTP_PORT
          value: '8080'
        - name: FOSSA_LOG_LEVEL
          value: INFO
        - name: FOSSA_API_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: token
              name: fossa-mcp-token
        image: localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0
        imagePullPolicy: Never
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 30
        name: server
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 3
          periodSeconds: 10
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 256Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 64Mi
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
        volumeMounts:
        # Nothing is expected to write to disk (the report tool deliberately
        # never does), so the root filesystem is read-only; /tmp is a scratch
        # mount in case a dependency wants one.
        - mountPath: /tmp
          name: tmp
      volumes:
      - emptyDir: {}
        name: tmp
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: fossa-mcp
  name: fossa-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: fossa-mcp
  type: ClusterIP

# Create the real secret out-of-band; never commit the actual token.
# A Full FOSSA API token (app.fossa.com -> Settings -> Integrations -> API):
#
#   kubectl -n ai create secret generic fossa-mcp-token \
#     --from-literal=token="$(tr -d '\r\n' < ~/Developer/keys/fossa/token.txt)"
#
# --from-file would keep the file's trailing newline in the value. The server
# strips surrounding whitespace from the token itself, so either form works, but
# the tr form keeps the stored secret byte-exact.
#
# Rotating: recreate the secret, then restart the deployment — the token is read
# once at process start.
#
#   kubectl -n ai delete secret fossa-mcp-token
#   kubectl -n ai create secret generic fossa-mcp-token --from-literal=token=<NEW>
#   kubectl -n ai rollout restart deploy/fossa-mcp
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: fossa-mcp-token
  namespace: ai
type: Opaque
stringData:
  token: REPLACE_ME

mcpo bridges MCP servers into Open WebUI as OpenAPI tools. Config points at the
in-cluster k8s MCP server, the docs-rag MCP server, and a systemd MCP on the host
(a raw IP — it runs on the node, not in the cluster). The mcpo `--api-key` in the
manifest is a placeholder — rotate it if the service ever leaves the trusted LAN.

`k8s-mcp-server.yaml` ships the ServiceAccount plus a cluster-scoped
ClusterRole/Binding limited to `get`/`list`/`watch`. That RBAC — not the
container's `--read-only` flag — is what actually makes the server read-only, so
keep the verbs as they are.

`docs-rag/` replaces the old `retrieval-tool` FastAPI service, which is gone from
the cluster: same Milvus-backed retrieval, but streamable-HTTP MCP instead of
OpenAPI, so external Claude/Cowork sessions can use it directly as well as
through mcpo. Companion repo: darthzen/ollama-code-mcp (Claude Code
→ Ollama delegation; runs stdio on the client, no cluster deployment needed).

# Decisions

Durable decisions for this project, with the reasoning. Each exists because the
"obvious" alternative looks correct and would be wrong. Read before changing any
of them.

---

## 1. Pin `mcp` to 1.28.x. Do not upgrade to 2.x yet.

**Decided 2026-07-29.**

`mcp[cli]>=1.28.1,<1.29`

MCP Python SDK **2.0.0 exists** (released 2026-07-28) and `FOSSA_MCP_IMPLEMENTATION_SCOPE.md`
§4.2/§5 instruct using it. We are deliberately not, because this server is published to Docker Hub
for external businesses to depend on, and 2.0.0 has no patch releases yet.

1.28.1 (released 2026-06-26) is the last 1.x with meaningful soak time. Note 1.29.0 shipped the
same day as 2.0.0 — also too new.

**Consequences:** `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP` is the correct API for this build, not `MCPServer`.
Scanners will flag the pin as behind 2.x. That is expected — do not auto-bump, and do not let a
dependency bot do it.

**Revisit when** 2.0.x has patch releases and real-world use. The migration is mechanical but not
trivial: 2.0.0 renames `fastmcp` → `mcpserver` and `FastMCP` → `MCPServer`, moves model fields to
snake_case (`read_only_hint`, `input_schema`), and relocates `Context` to
`mcp.server.mcpserver.context`. Keep the tool layer thin so the swap stays cheap.

---

## 2. Single-tenant only. Do not add multi-tenant auth.

**Decided 2026-07-29.**

Each operator runs their own container with their own `FOSSA_API_TOKEN`. One token per process,
supplied via environment at run time.

This is a **product constraint, not a technical limitation.** Multi-tenant FOSSA hosting is FOSSA,
Inc.'s own business and we are deliberately not building toward competing with it.

**Consequences:**

- `FOSSA_API_TOKEN` from the environment is the correct and complete auth model. Do not add
  `token_verifier`, OAuth, or per-request credential plumbing.
- `stdio` is the default transport and the intended deployment shape.
- `streamable-http` remains available but binds `127.0.0.1` by default. Keep it that way.
- `FossaClient` is a single lifespan-scoped instance with one connection pool. Correct *because* of
  this decision; it would be wrong under multi-tenancy.
- **The server executes every request with the single token it was started with.** Exposing the HTTP
  transport to multiple users grants them all of that token's access. This must stay documented in
  the README.

---

## 3. Apache-2.0, not MIT.

**Decided 2026-07-29.**

The full runtime dependency tree (36 packages at `mcp` 1.28.1) is permissive — MIT, BSD-2/3-Clause,
Apache-2.0, ISC, MIT-0, PSF-2.0 — with no GPL, LGPL, or AGPL. Every inbound license is compatible
with any permissive outbound license, so compatibility did not constrain the choice; it was made on
merit for distribution to businesses:

- **Explicit patent grant (§3)**, which MIT lacks. Enterprise legal review routinely flags that gap.
- **Explicit trademark disclaimer (§6)**, which matters here — see below.
- **NOTICE mechanism (§4)** carries the unofficial-tool disclaimer through redistribution.

**Obligations to keep meeting:**

- `certifi` is **MPL-2.0** — weak, file-level copyleft. It constrains nothing in our code (we do not
  modify it), but container images redistribute its binary, so its license text must ship in the
  image. Ship a consolidated third-party license file at a documented path.
- SUSE BCI base images carry SUSE's own terms, independent of our Apache-2.0 grant. Do not conflate
  them in documentation.

---

## 4. This is an unofficial tool. Keep saying so.

**Decided 2026-07-29.**

"FOSSA" is a trademark of FOSSA, Inc., used here nominatively to identify the API this software
talks to. The project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by FOSSA, Inc.

The disclaimer must appear in `NOTICE`, the README, the OCI image description, and the Docker Hub
overview. Do not adopt FOSSA branding, and do not attribute authorship to FOSSA — an earlier draft
of `pyproject.toml` listed `support@fossa.com` as the package author, which was incorrect and is
exactly the failure mode to avoid.

content.text:
Done. Two things block an actually-working deployment, and one of them I could only find by testing the real token.

## Blocker 1: the token is push-only, not Full

```
FOSSA API returned 403 ForbiddenError: This request is not permitted using a push-only API Token
```

That's the live smoke test against the real API using `~/Developer/keys/fossa/token.txt`. Push-only tokens are for `fossa analyze` uploads; every read endpoint this server uses rejects them. Spec §8 requires a **Full** token (app.fossa.com → Settings → Integrations → API). Once you have one:

```bash
kubectl -n ai delete secret fossa-mcp-token
kubectl -n ai create secret generic fossa-mcp-token \
  --from-literal=token="$(tr -d '\r\n' < ~/Developer/keys/fossa/token.txt)"
kubectl -n ai rollout restart deploy/fossa-mcp
```

Silver lining: this exercised the whole client path against production FOSSA — auth header, error-shape parsing, and an actionably worded 403 with no token leakage.

## Blocker 2: no image exists

`rashford/fossa-mcp` is not on Docker Hub (`object not found`), and there's no docker CLI on this machine, so I couldn't build it. I followed the `docs-rag-mcp` precedent instead — `localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0` with `imagePullPolicy: Never`, built and imported on the node:

```bash
docker build -t localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 .
docker save localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 | sudo k3s ctr -n k8s.io images import -
```

That avoids presuming a public Docker Hub push for a service that only serves your cluster. The manifest comment notes the one-line swap to `docker.io/rashford/fossa-mcp:0.1.0` + `IfNotPresent` if you do publish it.

## What I created in `lab-fleet/09-mcp/`

`fossa-mcp.yaml` (Deployment + ClusterIP Service) and `fossa-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt`, plus updates to the bundle `README.md` and the `fleet.yaml` header. It matches the house pattern — namespace `ai`, port 8080 like its peers, secret referenced by name and created out-of-band, example renamed `.txt` so Fleet never applies it. `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` passes against the live cluster.

Two places I went beyond the peers: real `/healthz` HTTP probes (this server has the endpoint, unlike the others, which use TCP or nothing), and a hardened `securityContext` — non-root uid 1000, all caps dropped, `readOnlyRootFilesystem` with an emptyDir `/tmp`, `RuntimeDefault` seccomp. The image already runs as uid 1000 and writes nothing to disk, so none of that costs anything.

**The security tradeoff you should know about:** a pod can't bind `127.0.0.1` and still be reachable through a Service, so this sets `FOSSA_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0` — contradicting DECISIONS.md §2. I recorded it there as the one sanctioned exception, valid *only* while the Service stays ClusterIP. Anything that can reach that ClusterIP inherits the token's full read access across your FOSSA org; there's no per-caller auth. No ingress, no LoadBalancer, without a proxy in front.

## Also

- **Token whitespace is now stripped** (`config.py`) — Secrets created with `--from-file` keep the file's trailing newline, which would have produced 401s that look like a bad token rather than a bad newline. Added `tests/test_config.py` covering it through to the Authorization header. Suite: 86 passed, 1 deselected; ruff, format, and pyright all clean.
- **The secret is already created** in `ai` (32 bytes, newline stripped, nothing echoed to this transcript) — but it holds the push-only token, so it'll 403 until you rotate it.
- **Nothing committed or applied.** Since Fleet reconciles from git, pushing now would deploy straight into `ImagePullBackOff` — I'd sequence it as: get a Full token → build and import the image → commit and push → let Fleet apply. Your call.
- The mcpo registration snippet for Open WebUI is documented in the bundle README but not applied, since editing that ConfigMap restarts mcpo.
- Unrelated: `git status` in lab-fleet shows ~40 pre-existing sync-conflict duplicates (`fleet 2.yaml`, `_helpers 3.tpl`, …). Not mine, but easy to sweep into a commit by accident.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# fossa-mcp — read-only MCP server for the FOSSA API (software composition
# analysis: projects, revisions, dependencies, licensing/vulnerability/quality
# issues, attribution reports). Nine tools, none of which mutate FOSSA state.
# Source: iCloud Developer/fossa-mcp (Apache-2.0, unofficial — not affiliated
# with FOSSA, Inc.).
#
# Image is built locally and imported into containerd, same as docs-rag-mcp:
#   docker build -t localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 .
#   docker save localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 | sudo k3s ctr -n k8s.io images import -
# Swap to docker.io/rashford/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 + pullPolicy IfNotPresent once that
# image is actually published (it is not, as of this commit).
#
# The FOSSA_API_TOKEN Secret is referenced by name and created out-of-band —
# see fossa-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: fossa-mcp
  name: fossa-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: fossa-mcp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fossa-mcp
    spec:
      containers:
      - args:
        - --transport
        - streamable-http
        env:
        # The image defaults to 127.0.0.1 by design (see the project's
        # DECISIONS.md §2). In a pod that would be unreachable through the
        # Service, so it binds the pod IP instead. Everything that can reach
        # this ClusterIP gets the full read access of the one token below —
        # there is no per-caller auth. Keep it ClusterIP-only.
        - name: FOSSA_HTTP_HOST
          value: 0.0.0.0
        # 8080 to match the other MCP servers in this namespace; the image
        # itself defaults to 8000.
        - name: FOSSA_HTTP_PORT
          value: '8080'
        - name: FOSSA_LOG_LEVEL
          value: INFO
        - name: FOSSA_API_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: token
              name: fossa-mcp-token
        image: localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0
        imagePullPolicy: Never
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 30
        name: server
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 3
          periodSeconds: 10
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 256Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 64Mi
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
        volumeMounts:
        # Nothing is expected to write to disk (the report tool deliberately
        # never does), so the root filesystem is read-only; /tmp is a scratch
        # mount in case a dependency wants one.
        - mountPath: /tmp
          name: tmp
      volumes:
      - emptyDir: {}
        name: tmp
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: fossa-mcp
  name: fossa-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: fossa-mcp
  type: ClusterIP

content.text:
Genuine defect found — and it means this Dockerfile has never successfully built:

```
error: variable expansion is not supported for --from, define a new stage with
FROM using ARG from global scope as a workaround
```

`COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}` can't interpolate. `FROM` can, so that's the fix:

input.old_string:
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Builder: resolve the locked dependency set and install the project with uv.
# Nothing in this stage ships in the runtime image except the venv and the
# generated third-party license file.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM ${PYTHON_BASE} AS builder

COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION} /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/
input.new_string:
# uv comes from its own published image. This has to be a named stage: `COPY
# --from=` does not expand variables, so `--from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}`
# fails to build, while `FROM` does expand ARGs from the global scope.
FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION} AS uv

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Builder: resolve the locked dependency set and install the project with uv.
# Nothing in this stage ships in the runtime image except the venv and the
# generated third-party license file.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM ${PYTHON_BASE} AS builder

COPY --from=uv /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/

ARG PYTHON_BASE=registry.suse.com/bci/python:3.13
ARG UV_VERSION=0.11.32

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Builder: resolve the locked dependency set and install the project with uv.
# Nothing in this stage ships in the runtime image except the venv and the
# generated third-party license file.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM ${PYTHON_BASE} AS builder

COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION} /uv /uvx /usr/local/bin/

ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 \
    UV_LINK_MODE=copy \
    UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never \
    UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv

WORKDIR /build

# Resolve and install dependencies first, from the lockfile alone, so this
# layer is cached independently of application source changes.
COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project

# Now install the project itself as a real (non-editable) package — the
# runtime stage ships only /opt/venv, not a copy of ./src to import against.
COPY src/ ./src/
COPY scripts/ ./scripts/
COPY README.md LICENSE NOTICE ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/uv \
    uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-editable

# Generate the consolidated third-party license file from what's actually
# installed in the venv (see DECISIONS.md §3 — certifi is MPL-2.0).
RUN /opt/venv/bin/python scripts/generate_third_party_licenses.py /build/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt

# build headers, no dev dependencies.

ARG BUILD_REVISION=unknown
ARG BUILD_VERSION=0.1.0
ARG BUILD_SOURCE=https://github.com/rashford/fossa-mcp

LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source=${BUILD_SOURCE} \
      org.opencontainers.image.version=${BUILD_VERSION} \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision=${BUILD_REVISION} \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses=Apache-2.0 \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="Read-only, single-tenant MCP server for the FOSSA API. Unofficial; not affiliated with FOSSA, Inc."

COPY --from=builder --chown=fossa:fossa /build/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt /app/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt

# fossa-mcp — read-only MCP server for the FOSSA API (software composition
# analysis: projects, revisions, dependencies, licensing/vulnerability/quality
# issues, attribution reports). Nine tools, none of which mutate FOSSA state.
# Source: iCloud Developer/fossa-mcp (Apache-2.0, unofficial — not affiliated
# with FOSSA, Inc.).
#
# Image is built locally and pushed to the in-cluster Harbor, same as
# ollama-exporter — so this needs the harbor-pull imagePullSecret, which is
# created out-of-band and is NOT in this repo:
#   docker build -t registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 .
#   docker push registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/fossa-mcp:0.1.0
#
# The FOSSA_API_TOKEN Secret is referenced by name and created out-of-band —
# see fossa-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: fossa-mcp
  name: fossa-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: fossa-mcp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fossa-mcp
    spec:
      containers:
      - args:
        - --transport
        - streamable-http
        env:
        # The image defaults to 127.0.0.1 by design (see the project's
        # DECISIONS.md §2). In a pod that would be unreachable through the
        # Service, so it binds the pod IP instead. Everything that can reach
        # this ClusterIP gets the full read access of the one token below —
        # there is no per-caller auth. Keep it ClusterIP-only.
        - name: FOSSA_HTTP_HOST
          value: 0.0.0.0
        # 8080 to match the other MCP servers in this namespace; the image
        # itself defaults to 8000.
        - name: FOSSA_HTTP_PORT
          value: '8080'
        - name: FOSSA_LOG_LEVEL
          value: INFO
        - name: FOSSA_API_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: token
              name: fossa-mcp-token
        image: localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0
        imagePullPolicy: Never
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 30
        name: server
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 3
          periodSeconds: 10
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 256Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 64Mi
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault

        - mountPath: /tmp

# 09 — MCP Layer

    kubectl apply -f k8s-mcp-server.yaml            # includes its read-only RBAC
    kubectl create secret generic github-mcp-token -n ai --from-literal=token=<PAT>   # see .example file
    kubectl apply -f github-mcp-server.yaml
    kubectl create secret generic fossa-mcp-token -n ai --from-literal=token=<FOSSA-TOKEN>  # see .example file
    kubectl apply -f fossa-mcp.yaml                 # needs the image imported first, below
    kubectl apply -f docs-rag/docs-rag-mcp.yaml     # see docs-rag/README.md
    kubectl apply -f mcpo.yaml

mcpo bridges MCP servers into Open WebUI as OpenAPI tools. Config points at the
in-cluster k8s MCP server, the docs-rag MCP server, and a systemd MCP on the host
(a raw IP — it runs on the node, not in the cluster). The mcpo `--api-key` in the
manifest is a placeholder — rotate it if the service ever leaves the trusted LAN.

`k8s-mcp-server.yaml` ships the ServiceAccount plus a cluster-scoped
ClusterRole/Binding limited to `get`/`list`/`watch`. That RBAC — not the
container's `--read-only` flag — is what actually makes the server read-only, so
keep the verbs as they are.

`fossa-mcp` is read-only software-composition-analysis access to FOSSA (projects,
revisions, dependencies, licensing/vulnerability/quality issues, attribution
reports — nine tools, none of which mutate FOSSA state). Own repo:
iCloud `Developer/fossa-mcp`, Apache-2.0, unofficial. Built locally like
docs-rag-mcp rather than pulled — `localhost/` + `pullPolicy: Never`:

    cd ~/Library/Mobile\ Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Developer/fossa-mcp
    docker build -t localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 .
    docker save localhost/fossa-mcp:0.1.0 | sudo k3s ctr -n k8s.io images import -
    kubectl -n ai rollout restart deploy/fossa-mcp

The single `FOSSA_API_TOKEN` in the Secret is the *only* access control: the
server does not authenticate callers, so anything that can reach the ClusterIP
inherits that token's full read access across the FOSSA org. Keep it ClusterIP —
no ingress, no LoadBalancer — and if it ever needs to leave the namespace, put an
authenticating proxy in front of it. It binds `0.0.0.0` in-pod only because
127.0.0.1 would be unreachable through the Service; see the project's
DECISIONS.md §2.

To surface it in Open WebUI, add it to the `mcpo-config` ConfigMap in `mcpo.yaml`
alongside the others and bump `config-revision`:

    "fossa": { "type": "streamable-http",
               "url": "http://fossa-mcp.ai.svc.cluster.local:8080/mcp" }

`docs-rag/` replaces the old `retrieval-tool` FastAPI service, which is gone from
the cluster: same Milvus-backed retrieval, but streamable-HTTP MCP instead of
OpenAPI, so external Claude/Cowork sessions can use it directly as well as
through mcpo. Companion repo: darthzen/ollama-code-mcp (Claude Code
→ Ollama delegation; runs stdio on the client, no cluster deployment needed).

content.text:
Built, pushed, and deployed — all in-cluster via the Kubernetes MCP.

**Answer to your original question:** no, it wasn't built, and I'd missed Harbor entirely. It's running in the `registry` namespace behind `registry.ash4d.com`, with the same `harbor-pull`/`registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/…` pattern `ollama-exporter` already uses. My manifest was pointing at `localhost/` + `pullPolicy: Never` — the `docs-rag-mcp` pattern — which was the wrong precedent to copy.

## The Dockerfile had never built

The first build failed on line 1:

```
error: variable expansion is not supported for --from, define a new stage with
FROM using ARG from global scope as a workaround
```

`COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}` doesn't interpolate. `FROM` does, so uv is now a named stage (`FROM ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION} AS uv` → `COPY --from=uv`). That's a fix in the repo's Dockerfile, not just in the build context. So the README's `docker run rashford/fossa-mcp:0.1` was doubly wrong: no such image, and the recipe couldn't produce one.

## How it got built

No Docker on this machine, so I ran a throwaway rootless BuildKit pod in `ai`, `kubectl cp`'d the staged context in, and had `buildctl` push straight to Harbor. I chose BuildKit over Kaniko specifically because it builds this Dockerfile as written — Kaniko would have forced me to strip the `RUN --mount=type=cache` lines, meaning the image wouldn't match the committed recipe. `robot$claude` turned out to have `pull,push` on the repository. Build pod is deleted.

```
registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/fossa-mcp:0.1.0
digest sha256:ea91d6bf8ff307b6a542aa81172e5607ad71e05285a3c54a4759eff6ee98f50c
```

## Deployed and verified

`deployment.apps/fossa-mcp 1/1`, `service/fossa-mcp ClusterIP 10.43.49.47:8080`. Verified from another pod: `/healthz` returns `ok`, and `POST /mcp` completes an MCP `initialize` handshake returning the nine-tool server. Readiness and liveness probes are passing against the real endpoint.

The manifest in `lab-fleet/09-mcp/fossa-mcp.yaml` now carries the Harbor image, `IfNotPresent`, and `imagePullSecrets: harbor-pull`, so what I applied by hand and what Fleet will reconcile are identical.

## Still outstanding

**The token is still push-only** — the pod is healthy, but every tool call will return `403 ForbiddenError: This request is not permitted using a push-only API Token` until you swap in a Full token and rerun the three commands from `fossa-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt`. That's the last thing between this and a working server.

Also unchanged: nothing is committed in either repo, and `mcpo` registration is documented but not applied (it would restart mcpo). Repo gates still green — 86 passed, 1 deselected.

content.text:
Hypothesis confirmed, and it exposes a structural bug: **`fossa_project_posture` cannot work with any input.**

| input form | `/v2/issues` (`scope[revision]`) | `/v2/revisions/{locator}/…` (path) |
|---|---|---|
| full locator `proj$sha` | 404 — FOSSA appends it to `scope[id]` | ✅ works |
| bare `sha` | ✅ works | 404 — path needs full locator |

Posture calls both families with one value, so it 404s either way. The unit tests pass because mocks accept any string. Fixing it — normalize once, accept either form:

input.new_string:
def bool_to_str(value: bool) -> str:
    """Convert a boolean to lowercase string for FOSSA API."""
    return "true" if value else "false"


def split_revision_locator(project_locator: str, revision_locator: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Return `(full_locator, revision_id)` for a project revision.

    FOSSA wants two different forms of the same revision depending on the
    endpoint, which is not obvious and is worth stating plainly:

    * Path parameters (`/v2/revisions/{locator}/...`) want the **full** locator,
      `git+github.com/acme/widget$abc123`.
    * `scope[revision]` on the issue endpoints wants the **bare revision id**,
      `abc123`. The server builds `scope[id]` + `$` + `scope[revision]` itself,
      so passing the full locator there yields a doubled string and a 404:
      `...widget$git+github.com/acme/widget$abc123`.

    Callers therefore accept either form from the model — the scope wording tells
    it to use the full locator — and normalize here.
    """
    prefix = f"{project_locator}$"
    if revision_locator.startswith(prefix):
        return revision_locator, revision_locator[len(prefix) :]
    return f"{project_locator}${revision_locator}", revision_locator

"""Posture-related tools for the FOSSA MCP server."""

import asyncio
from typing import Any, cast
from urllib.parse import quote

from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context

from ..client import FossaClient
from ..models import PostureInput, PostureResponse


async def project_posture(
    ctx: Context,
    project_locator: str,
    revision_locator: str,
    top_issue_count: int = 10,
) -> PostureResponse:
    """
    Provide one high-value, model-friendly view of a project revision's
    current FOSSA issue posture.

    This is a composite MCP workflow and is the centerpiece demo tool.
    """
    validated = PostureInput(
        project_locator=project_locator,
        revision_locator=revision_locator,
        top_issue_count=top_issue_count,
    )

    lifespan_ctx = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context
    client: FossaClient = lifespan_ctx["client"]

    scope_params = [
        ("scope[type]", "project"),
        ("scope[id]", validated.project_locator),
        ("scope[revision]", validated.revision_locator),
    ]

    async def issue_category_counts() -> tuple[int, Any]:
        return await client.request_json_with_status(
            "GET", "/v2/issues/categories", params=scope_params
        )

    async def issue_list(category: str, sort: str) -> tuple[int, Any]:
        params = [
            ("category", category),
            ("status", "active"),
            *scope_params,
            ("sort", sort),
            ("page", "1"),
            ("count", str(validated.top_issue_count)),
        ]
        return await client.request_json_with_status("GET", "/v2/issues", params=params)

    async def direct_dependencies_with_issues() -> Any:
        encoded_locator = quote(validated.revision_locator, safe="")
        params = [
            ("depth[]", "direct"),
            ("hasIssues[]", "hasIssues"),
            ("page", "1"),
            ("count", str(validated.top_issue_count)),
        ]
        return await client.request_json(
            "GET", f"/v2/revisions/{encoded_locator}/dependencies", params=params
        )

    # Exactly five independent upstream calls, executed concurrently.

from typing import Any, cast
from urllib.parse import quote

from mcp.server.fastmcp import Context

from ..client import FossaClient
from ..models import PostureInput, PostureResponse


async def project_posture(
    ctx: Context,
    project_locator: str,
    revision_locator: str,
    top_issue_count: int = 10,
) -> PostureResponse:
    """
    Provide one high-value, model-friendly view of a project revision's
    current FOSSA issue posture.

    This is a composite MCP workflow and is the centerpiece demo tool.
    """
    validated = PostureInput(
        project_locator=project_locator,
        revision_locator=revision_locator,
        top_issue_count=top_issue_count,
    )

    lifespan_ctx = ctx.request_context.lifespan_context
    client: FossaClient = lifespan_ctx["client"]

    # The issue endpoints and the dependencies endpoint want different forms of
    # the same revision (see split_revision_locator): bare id under
    # scope[revision], full locator in the path. This tool calls both, so it
    # needs both.
    full_revision_locator, revision_id = split_revision_locator(
        validated.project_locator, validated.revision_locator
    )

    scope_params = [
        ("scope[type]", "project"),
        ("scope[id]", validated.project_locator),
        ("scope[revision]", revision_id),
    ]

    async def issue_category_counts() -> tuple[int, Any]:
        return await client.request_json_with_status(
            "GET", "/v2/issues/categories", params=scope_params
        )

    async def issue_list(category: str, sort: str) -> tuple[int, Any]:
        params = [
            ("category", category),
            ("status", "active"),
            *scope_params,
            ("sort", sort),
            ("page", "1"),
            ("count", str(validated.top_issue_count)),
        ]
        return await client.request_json_with_status("GET", "/v2/issues", params=params)

            ("page", "1"),

    full locator as scope[revision] produces `...widget$git+github...$sha` and a
    404. Normalizing here is what keeps one MCP argument usable for both the
    issue endpoints and the path-parameter endpoints.

    assert rev_id == "4.17.21$build2"

async def test_posture_upstream_calls_run_concurrently(settings, respx_mock, make_context):
    """All five upstream calls must be in flight together, not issued serially.

    Each mocked handler waits until the fifth request has arrived. Sequential
    execution can never reach five in flight, so it fails on the barrier
    timeout instead of quietly passing.

    in_flight = 0
    all_arrived = asyncio.Event()

    async def barrier(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        nonlocal in_flight
        in_flight += 1
        if in_flight == 5:

        await asyncio.wait_for(all_arrived.wait(), timeout=5)
        if request.url.path.endswith("/categories"):

        if request.url.path.endswith("/dependencies"):

        return httpx.Response(200, json={"issues": []})

    ctx = make_context(client, settings)

    await client.aclose()

content.text:
The Full token works, and using it against production immediately exposed a bug the mocks couldn't catch.

## `fossa_project_posture` was broken — fixed

With a working token, posture 404'd on every call. FOSSA builds `scope[id]` + `$` + `scope[revision]` itself, so it had received `…lab-memory$…lab-memory$7ac44a8…`. The two endpoint families want *different* forms of the same revision:

| input | `/v2/issues` (`scope[revision]`) | `/v2/revisions/{locator}/…` (path) |
|---|---|---|
| full `proj$sha` | 404 — doubled | ✅ |
| bare `sha` | ✅ | 404 |

Posture calls both, so **no input value could work** — it was unusable regardless of what the caller passed. `fossa_list_issues` and `fossa_get_issue` had the same defect for the documented usage (spec §25 tells the model to pass the full locator, which is exactly the form that 404s).

The fix is one helper, `split_revision_locator`, which accepts either form and derives both: bare id for `scope[revision]` (including `scope[compareTo][revision]`), full locator for path parameters. Posture now echoes back the canonical full locator.

Verified against production, both forms giving identical results:

```
posture[full locator]: ok | state=complete | counts={'licensing': 0, 'vulnerability': 5, 'quality': 0} | direct_deps=1
posture[bare sha]:     ok | state=complete | counts={'licensing': 0, 'vulnerability': 5, 'quality': 0} | direct_deps=1
```

Three existing posture tests had encoded the buggy assumption (mocking `/v2/revisions/r/dependencies` where the real path is `/v2/revisions/p%24r/…`). I corrected them to the real contract rather than leaving them green against wrong behavior, and added regression tests that pin the asymmetry: parameterized over both input forms, asserting `scope[revision]` is the bare id while the dependencies path carries the full locator. 95 passed, ruff/format/pyright clean.

## Deployed

Rebuilt as `0.1.1` — I couldn't reuse `0.1.0`, since `IfNotPresent` wouldn't repull a mutated tag. Package version bumped to match.

```
registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/fossa-mcp:0.1.1
digest sha256:249e9fafe98d44d9262ed12af5acb70ceb3078284b2ac067ba3f6dafccdc830f
deployment.apps/fossa-mcp 1/1   service/fossa-mcp ClusterIP 10.43.49.47:8080
```

Secret rotated (32 bytes, no newline), deployment restarted, build pod deleted. `lab-fleet/09-mcp/fossa-mcp.yaml` and its README now reference `0.1.1`, so Fleet reconciles to exactly what's running.

Tools verified end-to-end through the cluster Service with a real MCP client: `fossa_list_projects` (3 projects), `fossa_list_issues`, `fossa_get_project`, `fossa_list_project_revisions`, `fossa_get_attribution_report` (750-char Markdown), and `fossa_project_posture` (5 real vulnerabilities on `lab-memory`).

## One usability note worth acting on

The project record returns its locator under `id`, not `locator` — `git+github.com/darthzen/lab-memory`. Chaining works, but a model has to guess that. This sharpens the outstanding review item about missing per-argument descriptions: the `project_locator` description should say the value comes from the `id` field of `fossa_list_projects` results, and `revision_locator` should note that revisions arrive nested under `branch`/`tag`, not as a flat list.

Still outstanding from the review: `SecretStr` for the token, per-argument descriptions, vendoring `spec/fossa-openapi.json`, the `AttributeError` on non-dict JSON error bodies, and `serverInfo.version` reporting `1.28.1` instead of `0.1.1`. Nothing is committed in either repo — `fossa-mcp` has the Dockerfile fix, the locator fix, and the version bump uncommitted; `lab-fleet` has the new bundle files untracked.

This is a good boundary to stop at — the session is long and the deployment is verified working. Want me to commit both repos, or hand off to a fresh session for the remaining review items?

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# fossa-mcp — read-only MCP server for the FOSSA API (software composition
# analysis: projects, revisions, dependencies, licensing/vulnerability/quality
# issues, attribution reports). Nine tools, none of which mutate FOSSA state.
# Source: iCloud Developer/fossa-mcp (Apache-2.0, unofficial — not affiliated
# with FOSSA, Inc.).
#
# Image is built locally and pushed to the in-cluster Harbor, same as
# ollama-exporter — so this needs the harbor-pull imagePullSecret, which is
# created out-of-band and is NOT in this repo:
#   docker build -t registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/fossa-mcp:0.1.1 .
#   docker push registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/fossa-mcp:0.1.1
#
# The FOSSA_API_TOKEN Secret is referenced by name and created out-of-band —
# see fossa-mcp-token.secret.example.yaml.txt.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    app: fossa-mcp
  name: fossa-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: fossa-mcp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: fossa-mcp
    spec:
      containers:
      - args:
        - --transport
        - streamable-http
        env:
        # The image defaults to 127.0.0.1 by design (see the project's
        # DECISIONS.md §2). In a pod that would be unreachable through the
        # Service, so it binds the pod IP instead. Everything that can reach
        # this ClusterIP gets the full read access of the one token below —
        # there is no per-caller auth. Keep it ClusterIP-only.
        - name: FOSSA_HTTP_HOST
          value: 0.0.0.0
        # 8080 to match the other MCP servers in this namespace; the image
        # itself defaults to 8000.
        - name: FOSSA_HTTP_PORT
          value: '8080'
        - name: FOSSA_LOG_LEVEL
          value: INFO
        - name: FOSSA_API_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              key: token
              name: fossa-mcp-token
        image: registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/fossa-mcp:0.1.1
        imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 30
        name: server
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 3
          periodSeconds: 10
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 256Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 64Mi
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
        volumeMounts:
        # Nothing is expected to write to disk (the report tool deliberately
        # never does), so the root filesystem is read-only; /tmp is a scratch
        # mount in case a dependency wants one.
        - mountPath: /tmp
          name: tmp
      imagePullSecrets:
      - name: harbor-pull
      volumes:
      - emptyDir: {}
        name: tmp
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  labels:
    app: fossa-mcp
  name: fossa-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 8080
    targetPort: 8080
  selector:
    app: fossa-mcp
  type: ClusterIP

# Decisions

Durable decisions for this project, with the reasoning. Each exists because the
"obvious" alternative looks correct and would be wrong. Read before changing any
of them.

---

## 1. Pin `mcp` to 1.28.x. Do not upgrade to 2.x yet.

**Decided 2026-07-29.**

`mcp[cli]>=1.28.1,<1.29`

MCP Python SDK **2.0.0 exists** (released 2026-07-28) and `FOSSA_MCP_IMPLEMENTATION_SCOPE.md`
§4.2/§5 instruct using it. We are deliberately not, because this server is published to Docker Hub
for external businesses to depend on, and 2.0.0 has no patch releases yet.

1.28.1 (released 2026-06-26) is the last 1.x with meaningful soak time. Note 1.29.0 shipped the
same day as 2.0.0 — also too new.

**Consequences:** `mcp.server.fastmcp.FastMCP` is the correct API for this build, not `MCPServer`.
Scanners will flag the pin as behind 2.x. That is expected — do not auto-bump, and do not let a
dependency bot do it.

**Revisit when** 2.0.x has patch releases and real-world use. The migration is mechanical but not
trivial: 2.0.0 renames `fastmcp` → `mcpserver` and `FastMCP` → `MCPServer`, moves model fields to
snake_case (`read_only_hint`, `input_schema`), and relocates `Context` to
`mcp.server.mcpserver.context`. Keep the tool layer thin so the swap stays cheap.

---

## 2. Single-tenant only. Do not add multi-tenant auth.

**Decided 2026-07-29.**

Each operator runs their own container with their own `FOSSA_API_TOKEN`. One token per process,
supplied via environment at run time.

This is a **product constraint, not a technical limitation.** Multi-tenant FOSSA hosting is FOSSA,
Inc.'s own business and we are deliberately not building toward competing with it.

**Consequences:**

- `FOSSA_API_TOKEN` from the environment is the correct and complete auth model. Do not add
  `token_verifier`, OAuth, or per-request credential plumbing.
- `stdio` is the default transport and the intended deployment shape.
- `streamable-http` remains available but binds `127.0.0.1` by default. Keep that default.
  **Kubernetes is the one sanctioned exception:** a pod must bind `0.0.0.0` or the Service can never
  reach it, so `lab-fleet/09-mcp/fossa-mcp.yaml` sets `FOSSA_HTTP_HOST=0.0.0.0`. That is only
  acceptable because the Service is ClusterIP-only inside a trusted namespace. Do not pair it with an
  Ingress or LoadBalancer without an authenticating proxy — see the next bullet for why.
- `FossaClient` is a single lifespan-scoped instance with one connection pool. Correct *because* of
  this decision; it would be wrong under multi-tenancy.
- **The server executes every request with the single token it was started with.** Exposing the HTTP
  transport to multiple users grants them all of that token's access. This must stay documented in
  the README.

---

## 3. Apache-2.0, not MIT.

**Decided 2026-07-29.**

The full runtime dependency tree (36 packages at `mcp` 1.28.1) is permissive — MIT, BSD-2/3-Clause,
Apache-2.0, ISC, MIT-0, PSF-2.0 — with no GPL, LGPL, or AGPL. Every inbound license is compatible
with any permissive outbound license, so compatibility did not constrain the choice; it was made on
merit for distribution to businesses:

- **Explicit patent grant (§3)**, which MIT lacks. Enterprise legal review routinely flags that gap.
- **Explicit trademark disclaimer (§6)**, which matters here — see below.
- **NOTICE mechanism (§4)** carries the unofficial-tool disclaimer through redistribution.

**Obligations to keep meeting:**

- `certifi` is **MPL-2.0** — weak, file-level copyleft. It constrains nothing in our code (we do not
  modify it), but container images redistribute its binary, so its license text must ship in the
  image. Ship a consolidated third-party license file at a documented path.
- SUSE BCI base images carry SUSE's own terms, independent of our Apache-2.0 grant. Do not conflate
  them in documentation.

---

## 4. This is an unofficial tool. Keep saying so.

**Decided 2026-07-29.**

"FOSSA" is a trademark of FOSSA, Inc., used here nominatively to identify the API this software
talks to. The project is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by FOSSA, Inc.

The disclaimer must appear in `NOTICE`, the README, the OCI image description, and the Docker Hub
overview. Do not adopt FOSSA branding, and do not attribute authorship to FOSSA — an earlier draft
of `pyproject.toml` listed `support@fossa.com` as the package author, which was incorrect and is
exactly the failure mode to avoid.

negative cache to expire. The durable fix is to stop hijacking port 53 for the
cluster's egress, or to forward `_acme-challenge.*.ash4d.com` upstream instead of
answering it locally.

    kubectl apply -f fossa-mcp.yaml                 # needs the image imported first, below
    kubectl apply -f docs-rag/docs-rag-mcp.yaml     # see docs-rag/README.md
    kubectl apply -f mcpo.yaml

mcpo bridges MCP servers into Open WebUI as OpenAPI tools. Config points at the
in-cluster k8s MCP server, the docs-rag MCP server, and a systemd MCP on the host
(a raw IP — it runs on the node, not in the cluster). The mcpo `--api-key` in the
manifest is a placeholder — rotate it if the service ever leaves the trusted LAN.

`k8s-mcp-server.yaml` ships the ServiceAccount plus a cluster-scoped
ClusterRole/Binding limited to `get`/`list`/`watch`. That RBAC — not the
container's `--read-only` flag — is what actually makes the server read-only, so
keep the verbs as they are.

`fossa-mcp` is read-only software-composition-analysis access to FOSSA (projects,
revisions, dependencies, licensing/vulnerability/quality issues, attribution
reports — nine tools, none of which mutate FOSSA state). Own repo:
iCloud `Developer/fossa-mcp`, Apache-2.0, unofficial. Image lives in the
in-cluster Harbor like ollama-exporter, so it needs the `harbor-pull`
imagePullSecret (created out-of-band, not in this repo):

    cd ~/Library/Mobile\ Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Developer/fossa-mcp
    docker build -t registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/fossa-mcp:0.1.1 .
    docker push registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/fossa-mcp:0.1.1
    kubectl -n ai rollout restart deploy/fossa-mcp

0.1.1 was built without a local Docker, using a throwaway rootless BuildKit pod
in `ai` that pushed straight to Harbor — `kubectl cp` the build context into
`/workspace/src`, then `buildctl build --output type=image,...,push=true`. Useful
if you ever need to rebuild from a machine with no container runtime.

The single `FOSSA_API_TOKEN` in the Secret is the *only* access control: the
server does not authenticate callers, so anything that can reach the ClusterIP
inherits that token's full read access across the FOSSA org. Keep it ClusterIP —
no ingress, no LoadBalancer — and if it ever needs to leave the namespace, put an
authenticating proxy in front of it. It binds `0.0.0.0` in-pod only because
127.0.0.1 would be unreachable through the Service; see the project's
DECISIONS.md §2.

content.text:
The ingress is set up and routing, but the TLS cert is stuck on something in your DNS — not on anything in the manifest.

## Ingress is live

`lab-fleet/09-mcp/fossa-mcp.yaml` now carries an Ingress following the `mcp-ollama` pattern: `letsencrypt-dns` DNS-01 issuer, `fossa-mcp-ash4d-tls` secret, and — matching its siblings — only `/mcp` is routed, so `/healthz` stays cluster-internal for the probes. Routing is confirmed working: a full MCP `initialize` handshake over `https://fossa-mcp.ash4d.com/mcp` returns the nine-tool server (with `-k`, since Traefik is still serving `CN=TRAEFIK DEFAULT CERT`).

## The cert is blocked by port-53 interception, not by cert-manager

cert-manager reports `DNS record ... not yet propagated` indefinitely. The record is fine — it's the lookup path that's broken:

- Cloudflare API: `_acme-challenge.fossa-mcp.ash4d.com` **exists**, created 05:23:15Z, in the correct zone (`ash4d.com`, served by `ed`/`jo.ns.cloudflare.com`).
- Cloudflare DoH *and* Google DoH (port 443): `Status: 0`, record resolves. **Publicly valid.**
- Any port-53 query returns NXDOMAIN — including, from inside a pod, a query aimed straight at `1.1.1.1`. A public resolver cannot legitimately deny a name that two DoH endpoints answer, so outbound 53 is being intercepted and answered locally.

So Let's Encrypt would validate this fine; only cert-manager's own self-check fails. `ash4d.com`'s SOA minimum is **1800s**, so the NXDOMAIN that got cached the instant the record was presented pins the check for up to 30 minutes. That also explains why `mcp-ollama` issued cleanly 35 minutes ago — same path, different timing.

It should clear itself shortly (challenge is ~10 min into the 30-minute window; cert-manager keeps retrying the same record name). I deliberately didn't touch cert-manager's args — it's a shared Fleet-managed component, and pointing `--dns01-recursive-nameservers` at public IPs wouldn't help anyway while port 53 is hijacked. The durable fix is on the network: stop intercepting 53 for the cluster's egress, or forward `_acme-challenge.*.ash4d.com` upstream instead of answering it locally. I documented the whole diagnosis, including the DoH one-liner to distinguish "record missing" from "cache stale", in the bundle README — it applies to every future cert in this lab.

To watch it land:

```bash
kubectl -n ai get certificate fossa-mcp-ash4d-tls -w
```

## Adding it to my MCP server list

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user fossa https://fossa-mcp.ash4d.com/mcp
```

`--scope user` makes it available in every project rather than just this one. Run it **after** the certificate goes `True` — Claude Code verifies TLS, so it'll fail against the Traefik default cert. Verify with `claude mcp list`, and the nine tools will appear as `mcp__fossa__fossa_*`.

I also amended `DECISIONS.md` §2, which I'd previously written as "no ingress, no LoadBalancer." It now records this LAN-scoped ingress as sanctioned, and states plainly what makes it acceptable — the private target address, nothing else. A Cloudflare Tunnel or a public A record crosses that line and needs authenticating middleware first, because the server still authenticates no callers.

Both repos remain uncommitted: `fossa-mcp` has the Dockerfile fix, the locator fix, the version bump, and the DECISIONS amendment; `lab-fleet` has the new bundle files and README. Given how long this session has run, I'd suggest committing both and then `/handoff` for the remaining review items (`SecretStr`, per-argument descriptions, vendoring the OpenAPI spec, the non-dict error-body `AttributeError`, and `serverInfo.version`). Want me to commit them now?

cd ~/Developer/lab-fleet/09-mcp && python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib
y = pathlib.Path("fossa-mcp.yaml"); s = y.read_text()
assert "kind: Ingress" not in s
s = s.replace("fossa-mcp:0.1.0", "fossa-mcp:0.1.1")
s = s.rstrip("\n") + """
---
# Reached from outside the cluster by Claude Code / Cowork sessions on the LAN.
# fossa-mcp.ash4d.com is a public Cloudflare record pointing at the private
# Traefik address (192.168.7.150), so it resolves everywhere but only connects
# from inside the network — same shape as mcp-ollama and mcp-memory.
#
# READ THIS BEFORE WIDENING IT: the server does not authenticate callers. Every
# request it serves uses the one Full FOSSA API token it started with, so
# whoever reaches this host has that token's read access to the whole FOSSA org.
# That is acceptable only while the target address stays private. Do not put it
# behind a Cloudflare Tunnel or a public A record without adding an
# authenticating middleware first (see the project's DECISIONS.md §2).
#
# Only /mcp is routed — /healthz stays cluster-internal for the probes.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-dns
  labels:
    app: fossa-mcp
  name: fossa-mcp
  namespace: ai
spec:
  rules:
  - host: fossa-mcp.ash4d.com
    http:
      paths:
      - backend:
          service:
            name: fossa-mcp
            port:
              number: 8080
        path: /mcp
        pathType: Prefix
  tls:
  - hosts:
    - fossa-mcp.ash4d.com
    secretName: fossa-mcp-ash4d-tls
"""
y.write_text(s)

r = pathlib.Path("README.md"); t = r.read_text()
t = t.replace("fossa-mcp:0.1.0", "fossa-mcp:0.1.1").replace(
    "0.1.0 was built without a local Docker", "0.1.1 was built without a local Docker")
old = """The single `FOSSA_API_TOKEN` in the Secret is the *only* access control: the
server does not authenticate callers, so anything that can reach the ClusterIP
inherits that token's full read access across the FOSSA org. Keep it ClusterIP —
no ingress, no LoadBalancer — and if it ever needs to leave the namespace, put an
authenticating proxy in front of it. It binds `0.0.0.0` in-pod only because
127.0.0.1 would be unreachable through the Service; see the project's
DECISIONS.md §2.
"""
new = """The single `FOSSA_API_TOKEN` in the Secret is the *only* access control: the
server does not authenticate callers, so anything that can reach it inherits that
token's full read access across the FOSSA org. It binds `0.0.0.0` in-pod only
because 127.0.0.1 would be unreachable through the Service; see the project's
DECISIONS.md §2.

Reached two ways: in-cluster clients use the ClusterIP name, and Claude Code /
Cowork sessions on the LAN use the Ingress at `https://fossa-mcp.ash4d.com/mcp`
(public Cloudflare record -> private Traefik address, so it resolves anywhere but
only connects from inside the network). Only `/mcp` is routed; `/healthz` stays
cluster-internal for the probes. That private target address is the whole security
boundary — a Cloudflare Tunnel or a public A record crosses it and needs an
authenticating middleware first.

    claude mcp add --transport http --scope user fossa https://fossa-mcp.ash4d.com/mcp

**DNS-01 gotcha, worth knowing for every cert in this lab:** the LAN intercepts
outbound port 53 — a pod querying `1.1.1.1` directly still gets the lab
resolver's answer. When cert-manager presents an `_acme-challenge` TXT record and
self-checks immediately, a miss gets negative-cached against the `ash4d.com` SOA
minimum (1800s), so issuance stalls for up to 30 minutes with
`DNS record ... not yet propagated` even though the record is live publicly.
Confirm with DoH, which cannot be intercepted:

    curl -H 'accept: application/dns-json' \\
      "https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=_acme-challenge.<host>.ash4d.com&type=TXT"

`Status: 0` means the record is fine and cert-manager just needs the negative
cache to expire. The durable fix is to stop hijacking port 53 for the cluster's
egress, or to forward `_acme-challenge.*.ash4d.com` upstream instead of answering
it locally.
"""
assert old in t
r.write_text(t.replace(old, new))
print("re-applied both files")

server does not authenticate callers, so anything that can reach the ClusterIP

Fix three contract defects found reviewing the implementation against the spec

fossa_get_project sent `refType`; getProject documents `ref_type`. FOSSA
silently ignores the unknown key, so ref_type="tag" resolved the ref as a
branch — a wrong answer rather than an error. Typed the parameter as RefType
too, so the published schema carries the enum instead of a bare string.

Unknown tool arguments were accepted and dropped. FastMCP 1.28 builds argument
models with pydantic's default extra="ignore", so a misspelled filter let a
model believe it had applied a constraint that never reached FOSSA. Tighten
every generated model to extra="forbid" and republish the schemas, which also
advertises additionalProperties: false.

The attribution report nested its result under `data`, while §13.9 defines
`format`/`content`/`truncated` at the top level, so a spec-following client
found none of them.

Tests: the mandated locator-encoding test asserted "%25" not in a locally
computed quote() result, which can never fail; it now asserts on the path httpx
actually put on the wire. Adds the missing coverage this review wanted —
revision comparison, ref_type, issue filter keys, attribution query map, posture
call parameters and concurrency, extra-argument rejection, and token absence
from tool output and logs. Live tests are deselected by default so `pytest`
cannot reach the network on a machine that exports FOSSA_API_TOKEN.

The conftest sys.path insert is explained rather than hand-waved: iCloud Drive
sets the macOS hidden flag on synced files and CPython 3.13+ skips hidden .pth
files, so an editable install inside iCloud is importable nowhere.

Build uv from a named stage so the image can actually build

`COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:${UV_VERSION}` does not expand variables:

    error: failed to solve: variable expansion is not supported for --from,
    define a new stage with FROM using ARG from global scope as a workaround

the README documenting a `docker run` against a published tag. FROM does expand
ARGs from the global scope, so uv becomes its own stage.

Send the revision form each FOSSA endpoint family actually expects

fossa_project_posture could not work with any input, and the issue tools failed
for the documented usage. FOSSA builds scope[id] + "$" + scope[revision] itself,
so scope[revision] wants the bare revision id while path parameters want the
full locator:

    full locator -> /v2/issues 404s: ...widget$git+github.com/acme/widget$abc123
    bare id      -> /v2/revisions/{locator}/... 404s: revision does not exist

Posture calls both families with one value, so it 404'd whichever form the
caller supplied. §25 tells the model to pass the full locator — exactly the form
the issue endpoints reject. split_revision_locator accepts either and derives
both, so one MCP argument stays usable everywhere; posture echoes the canonical
full locator back.

Only visible against the real API: the mocks accepted any string, and three
posture tests had encoded the wrong dependencies path. Those are corrected to
the real contract rather than left green, and the new tests pin the asymmetry
over both input forms.
